questions.stem: The Lok Sabha is also known as:
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha = 'House of the People' (Art 81) — lower / directly-elected house. Rajya Sabha = 'Council of States' (Art 80) — upper / indirectly-elected (by state MLAs). Together they form Parliament (Sansad).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: A NO-CONFIDENCE MOTION against the government is moved only in:
questions.explanation: No-confidence motion — only in Lok Sabha (reflects the government's accountability to the directly-elected house). Requires 50 supporting members for admission. If passed by majority, government falls. Rajya Sabha cannot move or decide no-confidence.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The FIRST Speaker of Lok Sabha was:
questions.explanation: G. V. Mavalankar — first Speaker (15 May 1952 to 27 February 1956, died in office). Called the 'Father of the Lok Sabha'. Meira Kumar — first WOMAN Speaker (2009-14). Current Speaker (2025): Om Birla (for 2nd consecutive term 2024).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: A 'ZERO HOUR' in Parliament refers to:

options.option_text: The first hour of the session (for prayers)
The time between the Question Hour and regular business, when MPs can raise urgent matters without notice
The final hour of a Bill's passage

questions.explanation: Zero Hour — starts at 12 noon (after 11 AM Question Hour). Informal — not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure. Indian innovation, since 1962. MPs raise matters of urgent public importance without prior notice. Speaker regulates who gets to speak.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The LEADER OF OPPOSITION (LoP) in Lok Sabha must lead a party that has at least how many seats (by convention)?

options.option_text: No minimum — just the largest opposition

questions.explanation: Convention: 10% seats (i.e., 55 in a 543-member Lok Sabha) required for recognition as LoP. Cabinet-minister status. Between 2014-19 and 2019-24, no party met this threshold → no formally recognised LoP. From June 2024, Rahul Gandhi (Congress) is LoP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The SPEAKER of the Lok Sabha presides over:

options.option_text: All proceedings of the Lok Sabha + certifies money bills

questions.explanation: Speaker — presides over Lok Sabha sittings; certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill (final + unquestionable decision); interprets rules; represents the House externally. Vote only in a tie (casting vote). Chair of joint session of Parliament.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The TERM of the Lok Sabha can be EXTENDED beyond 5 years during:

options.option_text: A proclamation of National Emergency under Art 352, by 1 year at a time

questions.explanation: Art 83(2) — during National Emergency (Art 352), Parliament may extend Lok Sabha by up to 1 year at a time (but not more than 6 months past the end of the Emergency). Used once — 1975-77 Emergency: Lok Sabha extended twice beyond its normal 5-year term.
